name_reason: Already follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=cursor, descriptor=move_up). No address residue. Caller fd2_wait_for_action_target_input dispatches it on scancode 0x48 (arrow up); body decrements cursor_world_y / scrolls window up. Name accurately reflects purpose and logic.
purpose: Up-arrow (scancode 0x48) battle cursor handler: move the cursor one tile up, scrolling the viewport at the top edge, and refresh the battle frame.
logic_summary: If cursor_world_y != 0 (not already at map top): when near the top viewport edge (cursor_screen_y < 2) and the view can still scroll up (view_window_origin_y != 0), decrement both cursor_world_y and view_window_origin_y (scroll the view up, cursor stays put on screen); otherwise decrement cursor_world_y and cursor_screen_y (step the cursor up one screen row) and, if no battle animation is active (anim_phase == 0), return early so the main loop redraws on its next tick. All other paths (scroll branch, animation-active inner step, and the world_y == 0 no-op) fall through to fd2_composite_battle_frame(0) to force an immediate redraw.

returns.semantics: No return value; effects are global state mutation (cursor/window position) and a battle-frame composite.

comment_original_issue: src comment block was a bare header (name + address + caller count) with no description of the function's behavior, scroll-vs-step branching, or the composite-redraw gating.
notes: void/void cdecl confirmed via signature (param_count 0) and decompile. Callers: fd2_game_main_loop, fd2_pan_cursor_to_tile_animated, fd2_wait_for_action_target_input (the last dispatches on scancode 0x48). Ghidra plate is detailed and consistent with the refined understanding (it uses a non-ASCII up-arrow glyph, but that is permitted in the Ghidra plate; src comment kept ASCII-only), so plate left untouched.
